meta.notes: The most instructive soft-cap row in the set. ETG has the exact profile the framework hunts for - farm-gate procurement in soft currencies across dozens of African markets against USD export receipts - and it is NOT a prospect, because it built three offshore treasury companies to solve it. The lesson for the tool: structural need and commercial opportunity are different things, and only research at this depth distinguishes them. A scraper would rank ETG in the top five. v1.3 UPDATE: reclassified from exclusion to narrow-pitch prospect. The offshore treasury companies solve ETG's treasury problem; they do not solve farm-gate collection and payout across dozens of African markets. Still the worked example on the demo page, but the lesson changes from 'the tool knows when to exclude' to 'the tool knows WHICH PRODUCT to pitch' - which is a better lesson.

Per Kindred Ventures: with 'Tala in a Box', lending capital moves across stablecoin rails, and Tala has built local off-ramp pathways - neighbourhood convenience stores, partner banks, Tala mobile wallets - so customers can hold value digitally and convert to local currency when needed. money_movement.supplier_geography: international terminal suppliers historically; now non-Nigerian payment partners
money_movement.payment_frequency: recurring - FX payments on demand for third parties

tier1_cross_border_payments.source: PRIMARY INTERVIEW, Aug 2026 - treasury analyst: FX payment for third parties is now one of Nomba's major lines of business; pays for corporate and retail on demand

tier1_usd_liquidity.source: PRIMARY INTERVIEW - holds liquidity directly in USD and GBP and pays from it; maintains multiple offshore accounts

tier1_multi_currency_obligations.source: PRIMARY INTERVIEW - operations across NGN, USD and GBP

tier1_multi_market_collection.source: PRIMARY INTERVIEW - collects from Nigerian corporates and retail for onward FX payment

tier2_disclosed_pain.source: PRIMARY INTERVIEW - analyst states cross-border payment has not been cracked; even when the process runs smoothly it still takes time to land. Local dom account settlement T+1 to T+3; bank processing within the hour or end of day depending on relationship pressure rather than anything the company controls.

tier2_multi_entity.source: PRIMARY INTERVIEW - multiple offshore accounts alongside the Nigerian entity

tier2_multiple_local_rails.source: PRIMARY INTERVIEW - pays FX for corporate and retail customers across channels

tier2_compliance_friction.source: PRIMARY INTERVIEW - the partners actually processing payments are mostly not Nigerian entities and add a compliance layer demanding CAC documents, payer identity and source of funds. Analyst: our people here often don't have what is being asked for. Payments stall on eligibility, not price.

product_gates.gate_note: Sells FX payment services onward to corporates and retail. Triggers the FX-provider signature.

tier0_flags.tier0_note: NOT A COMPETITOR under the same-buyer test. Nomba sells FX payment services to Nigerian corporates and retail; it does not sell cross-border settlement infrastructure to businesses building on top of it. Its own rails are borrowed - the processing partners are non-Nigerian entities. Same shape as Coinbase: competes on one layer, buys underneath on another.

urgency.note: FX became a major line of business recently and is growing; expansion into USD and GBP operations is what removed the third-party payer dependency.

meta.evidence_type: PRIMARY - first-hand interview with a serving treasury analyst, August 2026
meta.notes: The only row in the dataset built from primary research rather than public sources. PATTERN: solved its own FX problem by becoming an FX provider. Not treasury-solved, not a competitor - a company running an FX line on partner rails with its own customers to serve. THE PITCH: not treasury tooling. Sell Nomba the ability to promise its own customers faster settlement and a regulated local compliance counterparty, replacing foreign processors that demand documents Nigerian companies often cannot produce. Interview also supplies the simulator's core numbers: local dom T+1 to T+3, US offshore paying into the US same day within hours, bank processing within the hour or end of day depending on relationship.
